title: GALEX finds a hot, offset, quasar-like UV source in 13 percent of Gaia dwarfs with extreme 12 um excess, 27 times the control rate and also in centroid-clean stars; deep dimmers lack it
abstract: Question: Do ultraviolet and X-ray data show hidden sources of the extreme 12 um excess of Gaia DR3 field dwarfs, the population linked to deep dust dimming, and are the unblended excess stars and the dimmers magnetically young? Approach: For 951 confirmed excess stars and 7,922 matched field controls (from a prior centroid study), 93 dimmers with 2,268 parallax-matched controls and 3,230 members of five young clusters, we used GALEX GR6/7 NUV and FUV, Gaia DR3 variability classes, eRASS1 coronal X-ray identifications, SDSS spectra and ZTF light curves. Each star is compared with its own controls by permutation tests. A UV excess means NUV - G more than 1 mag bluer than the UV-brightest decile of Pleiades and Praesepe members. Results: 83 of 678 testable excess stars have a UV excess against 16.2 expected (odds ratio 27, 21-35); for centroid-clean stars with field kinematics, 13 of 83 against 2.4. The UV source has quasar-like FUV - NUV (median 0.67; SDSS quasars 0.82) and NUV - W3(excess) (9.8; quasars 9.3), it is offset by 1.26 arcsec (controls 0.71), and three UV-excess M and K dwarfs with SDSS spectra have no H-alpha emission. Only 2 of 46 stars with variable NEOWISE hot dust have a UV excess. Without UV-excess stars, unblended stars are not brighter in NUV than controls. Gaia spot classes show that unblended stars with young-like kinematics are active (5 against 1.9), while at most 8-37 percent (95 percent, calibrator-dependent) of those with field kinematics have 120-670 Myr-like activity. No campaign dimmer is a spot-class, X-ray or ZTF rotation source; Gaia20cdd, G4466 and G2874 have normal NUV, but G2870 is about 3 mag too bright in NUV with red FUV - NUV. Conclusion: chance background quasars very probably make at least 13 percent of the extreme-dust sample and about 15 percent of its centroid-clean field-kinematics stars, so the genuine mature extreme-dust rate is lower; the known deep dimmers are UV-clean and look old. Limitations: broadband UV only, no quasar spectra, AIS depth (NUV about 21), calibrator-dependent activity bounds.
